record.title: Burundi COVID entry restriction from Rwanda
record.scope: Burundi–Rwanda land border, Ruhwa specifically corroborated
record.movement: Passengers arriving from Rwanda, including Congolese transit travellers and schoolchildren.
record.exceptions: Air passengers reported continuing on 15 March. Cargo policy differed by phase: The New Times reported restored cargo movement on 13 April 2020, while IWACU reports a foreign-ministry note dated 14 April. Neither fixes a passenger reopening.
record.imposing_authority: Burundian immigration authorities implementing reported verbal order
record.enforcement: Contemporaneous testimony in SOS and Radio Okapi reports denied passenger entry. Formal written Burundi order not retrieved; source independence is not assumed merely from publisher count.
record.official_rationale: Response to first reported COVID-19 cases in Rwanda.
record.uncertainty: Distinct tightening within earlier political restrictions GL02; no separate reopening date established. Avoid double-counting simultaneous causes as additional full closures. Later freight restrictions were uneven: an IWACU account of Rwanda’s 30 March note reports blocked trucks and admissions at different posts. Another IWACU report describes a 14 April goods-vehicle relaxation. Neither identifies the separate passenger endpoint. An opened New Times report dated 13 April 2020 already describes resumed cargo movement through government/FEAFFA statements. Keep this earlier reporting distinct from the 14 April note reported by IWACU; exact implementation across crossings remains unresolved. A substantially matching Egypt SIS indexed article displayed as 28 June 2022 is not evidence of a separate 2022 episode.

historical.duration_note: Chronology contains unresolved or conflicting claims; no precise interval calculated
